heroHeadline: Iran MOU Signed June 17, Oil Crashes ~11%; ECB (2.25%) and BOJ (1.00%) Deliver Hikes; Warsh's First FOMC Turns Hawkish; Goldman Confirms 15% Recession Odds; China Q2 GDP Slows to 4.3%; Section 122 Tariff Cliff 8 Days Away
heroSubtitle: The triple central bank week long flagged as the year's most consequential macro event resolved June 11-17: the ECB hiked to 2.25% (first since July 2023), the BOJ hiked to 1.00% (highest since 1995), and Kevin Warsh's first FOMC as Fed Chair held rates at 3.50-3.75% with a hawkish dot plot — the 2026 median projection rose to 3.8% from 3.4%, implying a hike rather than a cut. But the dominant story of the window was the US-Iran MOU, formally signed June 17: Iran reopened the Strait of Hormuz, the US lifted its naval blockade, and Brent crude crashed roughly 11% same-day, falling further to around $73/barrel by early July — down about 40% from April's war-peak of $118. Goldman Sachs confirmed its 12-month US recession probability at 15% on June 22, calling it the firm's 'long-term norm' now that the acute war-risk premium has been retired. US data since has been mixed: May PCE hit a three-year-high 4.1% headline (June 25), June's jobs report showed a sharp slowdown to +57,000 payrolls (July 2, though unemployment fell to 4.2% on lower participation), and June CPI cooled to 3.5% (July 14), suggesting the inflation peak has passed. The S&P 500 closed H1 2026 up 9.6% — its best first half since 2020. Renewed downside risk is building elsewhere: China's Q2 GDP grew just 4.3%, the slowest pace in roughly 3.5 years, and the IMF's July World Economic Outlook Update revised global headline inflation up to 4.7%, saying disinflation had 'stalled.' The most immediate risk ahead is the Section 122 tariff cliff, now just 8 days away (July 24): no Congressional extension has been reported, and USTR's Section 301 fallback tariffs on 60 economies — which closed their comment period July 6 and held a hearing July 7 — face a standard 30-day pre-effect rulemaking clock that may not clear in time, raising the prospect of a tariff-revenue coverage gap just before the next (non-SEP) FOMC meets July 28-29.

Critical path: Section 122 cliff July 24 (8 days) → next FOMC July 28-29 (non-SEP) → China Politburo meeting (late July, stimulus watch).
